narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your current job. Because this probability tips just over 50%, the system has flagged you as likely to depart and therefore recommended against offering you a promotion at this time.

Three aspects of your profile most strongly shaped this outlook. First, the fact that you have not received other job offers while working here actually pulled the prediction toward staying; most employees the model expects to remain also report no external opportunities. Second, having spent 6–10 years in your current role (longer than the majority of employees predicted to stay) worked against you, as the model sees this length of tenure in one organization as a signal that people often begin looking elsewhere. Third, your overall career experience of 6–10 years pushed the prediction further toward leaving. While many who are expected to stay have only 1–5 years of total experience, the model has learned that mid-career professionals with your profile tend to explore new opportunities.

Taken together, the absence of outside offers provided some reassurance, but your tenure both inside and outside the company outweighed that positive signal.

The organization should discuss your long-term goals with you and explore whether additional responsibilities, clearer growth paths, or changes in role could increase your sense of future opportunity here. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more compelling. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook for both sides. (248 words)
